key_insight: For sufficiently hard tasks, any two minimal DNN solutions that are weakly aligned by affine mappings will also strongly align in their privileged axes, with alignment propagating through the network hierarchy.
engineering_relevance: This suggests model comparison and representation matching may be more robust than expected, because task pressure can make convergent internal structure emerge across different networks.
method: Formalize contravariance for minimal DNN solutions on hard tasks.
Show weak affine alignment implies strong alignment of privileged axes.
Demonstrate that alignment zippers upward through layers during end-to-end optimization.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents theoretical results rather than a new empirical dataset, using hard-task minimal-solution arguments to support the alignment claims.
watch_item: The conclusion may depend on the assumptions of sufficiently hard tasks and minimal solutions, so it may not directly extend to easier tasks or non-minimal models.
paper_title: Contravariance Theory: Strong Alignment for Minimal Solutions to Hard Tasks
